original_question: Develop a standard notation for Painleve transcendents that takes into account the wide variety of qualitatively different solutions that the Painleve equations possess and can distinguish those different solution families clearly.
target_in_paper: Section 3, Open Problem 3.1: "Develop a notation for the Painlevé transcendents which takes into account the wide variety of solutions the Painlevé equations have."
correct_elements: Your draft is very close to the paper’s actual target. It correctly identifies that the problem is about creating a notation for Painlevé transcendents and correctly emphasizes that the notation must reflect the existence of many qualitatively different solution families rather than treating all solutions as interchangeable.
missing_details: The paper’s scope is the Painlevé transcendents as solutions of the six Painlevé equations PI–PVI, introduced in Section 1 as equations (1.1)–(1.6), with their usual equation parameters.

The official formulation is not just any notation, but an agreed notation for the Painlevé transcendents, motivated by the fact that, unlike other special functions in the DLMF, they currently have no dedicated standard notation.

The nearby context explains why this is difficult: unlike linear second-order equations, Painlevé equations do not have a finite set of representative solutions analogous to a basis, so the notation must separate genuinely different solution families.

Section 3 makes explicit, via PII, what 'wide variety' means: the notation should be able to distinguish at least families such as the general two-parameter transcendental solution, Ablowitz–Segur, Hastings–McLeod, singular, pure-imaginary and complex Ablowitz–Segur, quasi-Ablowitz–Segur, quasi-Hastings–McLeod, special-function, rational, tronquée, and tri-tronquée solutions.

The paper also states a hidden structural constraint: the full solution set forms a transcendental structure 'without any global coordinates' that could act as universal markers, so the refined question should not assume a simple global parametrization of all solutions.
To be fully stand-alone, the question should say explicitly that 'Painlevé transcendents' means solutions w(z) of PI–PVI, rather than assuming the reader knows the term from context.
There are no ambient ring/field, degree, homogeneity, nilpotency, or 'for all sufficiently large m' hypotheses in this problem; importing such conditions would be unfaithful to the paper.
refined_question: Can one devise an agreed notation for the Painlevé transcendents—that is, for solutions w(z) of the six Painlevé equations PI–PVI with their standard parameters—that distinguishes the qualitatively different solution families each equation possesses, rather than treating the nonlinear equations as if they had only a few representative solutions; in particular, can such a notation separate the kinds of families illustrated in Section 3 for PII (general transcendental, Ablowitz–Segur, Hastings–McLeod, singular and complex variants, quasi-Ablowitz–Segur, quasi-Hastings–McLeod, special-function, rational, tronquée, and tri-tronquée solutions) despite the absence of natural global coordinates on the full solution space?
justification: The draft is essentially a paraphrase of the paper’s official statement in Open Problem 3.1, so the target is clear. The necessary sharpening comes from nearby context in Section 3: Clarkson explains that there is currently no special notation for Painlevé transcendents in the DLMF, that nonlinear Painlevé equations do not admit a finite set of representative solutions as linear equations do, and that even for PII there are many analytically distinct families of solutions. He also notes that the full solution space lacks global coordinates that could serve as universal labels. Therefore the paper-faithful refinement should stay narrowly focused on creating notation for solutions of PI–PVI that is sensitive to distinct solution families, without broadening the problem into a general classification or computational program.
